document_check.note: Zhao A, Fang F, Li B, Chen Y, Qiu Y, Wu Y, Xu W and Deng Y (2021) Visual Abnormalities Associate With Hippocampus in Mild Cognitive Impairment and Early Alzheimer's Disease. Front. Aging Neurosci. 12:597491, doi 10.3389/fnagi.2020.597491. The title matches the summaries.md header for Paper 933. The document is a single-centre study of 23 MCI, 17 AD and 19 normal controls (Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai) using PVEP, flash ERG, OCT and 3T MRI. Table 2 (page 5) reports m-RNFL thickness of 96.76 (7.30) um in NC and 88.65 (9.81) um in MCI (MCI vs NC P = 0.011, text page 5). It also reports rod cone response latency of 41.36 vs 50.50 ms (MCI vs NC P = 0.003, text page 4). The cited numbers match.

cited_result: Between-group comparison at a single time point of macular RNFL thickness (Stratus OCT; NC 96.76 vs MCI 88.65 um, P = 0.011) and flash-ERG latency (dark-adapted rod cone response latency NC 41.36 vs MCI 50.50 ms, P = 0.003) in 23 amnestic MCI patients against 19 age-, sex- and education-matched cognitively normal controls. One-way ANOVA with a pairwise threshold of 0.05/3 = 0.017.
tool_reason: The cited result compares OCT and flash-ERG measures taken at one time point between MCI patients and normal controls. It is a group comparison, not a model, an accuracy estimate against a reference standard, or a prognostic association, so the JBI analytical cross-sectional checklist applies. The paper calls itself cross-sectional and every measure was taken concurrently. Its clinic-case versus matched-community-control sampling is noted under items 2, 3 and 6.

domains.domain: Item 1: Criteria for inclusion clearly defined
domains.rationale: MCI was defined by the Mayo Clinic criteria (amnestic, Petersen 2004). Controls needed an MMSE of 28 or more and no memory complaint. Neurological, systemic and ocular exclusions are listed, including ocular disease, high refractive error and prior ophthalmic surgery.

signalling.question: Were the criteria for inclusion in the sample clearly defined?
signalling.quote: MCI with deﬁcits in memory function were diagnosed according to the Mayo Clinic criteria (Petersen, 2004).

signalling.question: Were inclusion criteria stated for the control group?
signalling.quote: Inclusion criteria for normal controls required a MMSE score ≥28 without any memory-related complaint.

signalling.question: Were ocular exclusion criteria relevant to OCT and ERG stated?
signalling.quote: Individuals with any ocular disease, high refractive error, systemic disease aﬀecting vision or history of ophthalmic surgery were excluded.

domains.domain: Item 2: Study subjects and setting described in detail
domains.rationale: The setting (Ruijin Hospital neurology clinic, Shanghai), the source of controls (local community) and group demographics (Table 1) are reported. Two gaps remain. The patient sampling method (consecutive or convenience) is not stated. The stated enrolment period ends in December 2020, after the manuscript was received in August 2020. These are reporting gaps and do not undermine the description of who was studied.

signalling.question: Were the study subjects and the setting described in detail?
signalling.quote: Participants (N = 59) in this study were enrolled at the neurology clinic of Ruijin Hospital

signalling.question: Is the source of the control group stated?
signalling.quote: The cognitively normal participants were age-, sex-, and education-matched and were recruited from the local community in Shanghai.

signalling.question: Are participant characteristics tabulated by group?
signalling.quote: TABLE 1 | Demographic characteristics of all participants.

signalling.question: Is the patient sampling method (consecutive, random or convenience) stated?
signalling.quote: Looked in Patients Enrolment and Results for how patients were selected from the clinic; the text states only where they were enrolled and the period.

signalling.question: Is the reported enrolment period internally consistent?
signalling.quote: from September 2016 to December 2020.

domains.domain: Item 3: Exposure (diagnostic group membership) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: All participants received the same neuropsychological battery from a specialist, and MCI followed standard clinical criteria. However, the two groups were classified by different rules. MCI was a clinical judgement in which the 1.5 SD guideline is not a cut-off. Controls needed an MMSE of 28 or more and no complaint. The stated MoCA cut-off for MCI (24 or below) sits at the control group's mean MoCA (24.89, SD 2.13), so some controls would score in the MCI range on MoCA. No amyloid or tau markers were available. Misclassification between the MCI and control groups cannot be ruled out.

signalling.question: Was group membership established in a valid and reliable way for all groups?
signalling.quote: Age- and education-adjusted scores falling 1.5 standard deviations below that expected for age and education level may indicate MCI but these are considered as guidelines rather than diagnostic cut-oﬀs.

signalling.question: Were controls assessed with the same battery as patients?
signalling.quote: Specialists assessed cognitive ability in all participants utilizing Mini-Mental State Examination

signalling.question: Were the same classification thresholds applied to patients and controls?
signalling.quote: We used MoCA cut-oﬀ scores of ≤24 points for MCI and ≤22 points for dementia

signalling.question: Do the control group's scores fall clear of the stated MCI threshold?
Was the MCI classification supported by pathological biomarkers?
signalling.quote: Owing to the lack of Aβ or Tau-related markers, we were unable to analyze the relationship between those pathological markers and ocular measurements

domains.domain: Item 4: Objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition
domains.rationale: MCI was diagnosed by the published Mayo Clinic (Petersen 2004) criteria, whose components are listed. AD was diagnosed by NIA-AA criteria. The concerns about how consistently these were applied across groups are recorded under item 3.

signalling.question: Were objective, standard criteria used for measurement of the condition?
signalling.quote: The criteria include subjective memory complaint corroborated by an informant together with preserved everyday activities, a memory impairment based on a standard neuropsychological test

domains.rationale: Age, sex, education or cognitive reserve, and APOE4 status are named as confounders. Ocular conditions that affect OCT and ERG (ocular disease, high refractive error, systemic disease affecting vision, ophthalmic surgery) are recognised through exclusion.

signalling.question: Were confounding factors identified?
signalling.quote: after adjusting for confounding factors including age, sex, cognitive reserve, and APOE4 status.

signalling.question: Were ocular factors that could affect OCT and ERG recognised?
signalling.quote: Individuals with any ocular disease, high refractive error, systemic disease aﬀecting vision or history of ophthalmic surgery were excluded.

domains.domain: Item 6: Strategies to deal with confounding stated
domains.rationale: Two design strategies are stated: controls matched at group level on age, sex and education, and restriction by ocular exclusions. The groups did not differ significantly on age, sex, education or APOE4. The group comparison itself was an unadjusted ANOVA, and statistical adjustment was applied only to the correlation and regression analyses. Residual confounding by age (NC 66.63 vs MCI 68.43 years) and by ocular factors not tabulated (refractive error was restricted only as 'high') is possible but not shown.

signalling.question: Were strategies to deal with confounding factors stated?
signalling.quote: The cognitively normal participants were age-, sex-, and education-matched

signalling.question: Were the groups comparable on the matched factors?
signalling.quote: There was no signiﬁcant diﬀerence in age, sex, years of education and APOE 4 carrier status among three groups.

signalling.question: Was the between-group comparison of the cited ocular measures adjusted for confounders?
signalling.quote: One-way ANOVAs were used to compare group diﬀerences in demographic and clinical variables between the three groups

domains.domain: Item 7: Outcomes (OCT m-RNFL thickness and flash-ERG latency) measured validly and reliably
domains.rationale: Both measures used standard equipment and protocols: Stratus OCT 3000 with fixation and signal monitoring and repeat scans, and LKC UTAS-E 3000 Ganzfeld ERG after dilation and dark adaptation. However, the m-RNFL measure is described ambiguously: the text mentions central-ring retinal thickness and hemiretinal RNFL without naming the segmentation. No repeatability data are given. Nothing states that the OCT or ERG examiners were unaware of diagnostic group, and ERG peak latencies may involve operator marking.

signalling.question: Were the outcomes measured with standard equipment and protocols?
signalling.quote: All participants underwent the OCT examination using the STRATUS OCT Model 3000 (Carl Zeiss Meditec, Inc., Dublin, California, USA).

signalling.question: Was the ERG recorded under a standard protocol?
signalling.quote: Standard Ganzfeld scotopic (dark-adapted) and photopic (light- adapted) ERGs were obtained by specialists after pupillary dilation.

signalling.question: Was image quality controlled?
signalling.quote: Scans were repeated until an image of satisfying quality was obtained.

signalling.question: Was the derivation of the m-RNFL measure described unambiguously?
signalling.quote: The retinal mapping software was used to calculate the average retinal thickness of the central ring. All eyes were scanned in a radial-spoked pattern centered on the foveola with the scan length of 6 mm. The mean and standard deviations of the macular RNFL (m-RNFL) were calculated in superior, inferior hemiretina.

signalling.question: Were the OCT and ERG examiners unaware of participants' diagnostic group?
signalling.quote: Looked in the OCT, PVEP and FERG Methods subsections and the Statistical Analysis for any statement on masking of examiners to diagnosis; none found.

signalling.question: Was measurement reliability (repeatability) reported, or how repeated ERG recordings were combined?
signalling.quote: Three ERG recordings were obtained per stimulus intensity.

domains.rationale: The unit of analysis handles inter-eye correlation (two eyes averaged), all 59 participants are analysed, and F, df and effect sizes are reported. Several things are missing: the post hoc procedure is not named, distributional checks are not reported, and no sample size justification is given for a small sample (23 vs 19). The Bonferroni divisor of 3 covers the three pairwise comparisons only, not the 16 ocular measures in Table 2. Both cited MCI vs control differences (P = 0.011 and P = 0.003) pass the per-outcome threshold of 0.017 but not a correction across outcomes (0.05/48, about 0.001). The analysis type is appropriate, but these gaps prevent a Yes.

signalling.question: Was the unit of analysis appropriate given two eyes per participant?
signalling.quote: Both eyes for each subject were examined and the average of these measurements was taken for the both eyes.

signalling.question: Was the between-group test fully specified, including the post hoc procedure and assumption checks?
signalling.quote: For multiple comparisons of demographic characteristics, ocular measurements and hippocampus volumes among AD, MCI, and cognitively normal group, the adjusted P-value required for signiﬁcance is 0.05/3 = 0.017.

signalling.question: Was multiplicity across the many ocular outcomes addressed?
signalling.quote: MCI patients showed signiﬁcantly thinner m-RNFL compared to normal individuals (P = 0.011) as well.

signalling.question: Does the flash-ERG MCI vs control difference rest on a single comparison among many?
signalling.quote: delayed rod cone response latency time was found in both MCI (P = 0.003) and AD (P = 0.003) patients compared to normal controls.

signalling.question: Was the sample size justified?
signalling.quote: In the current cross-sectional study we have enrolled relatively small sample size

signalling.question: Were all enrolled participants included in the analysis?
signalling.quote: In this research, 19 cognitively normal controls, 23 MCI patients and 17 AD patients were included.

overall: Some concerns (JBI analytical cross-sectional: items 3, 7 and 8 Unclear; no item No)
overall_rationale:
Under the review's JBI rule, none of items 5 to 8 is No, so the rating is not high. It is not low either, because items 3, 7 and 8 are Unclear. Confounders are identified and addressed by matching and ocular exclusions. The concerns are these:
- Cases came from a clinic and controls from the community, and the two groups were classified by different rules. The controls' mean MoCA sits at the stated MCI cut-off.
- The OCT m-RNFL measure is specified ambiguously, with no masking of examiners and no reliability data.
- The group comparison is an unadjusted ANOVA in a small sample, with no correction across the 16 ocular measures.
Both cited MCI vs control differences pass only the per-outcome threshold of 0.017.

applicability.rationale: Single tertiary neurology clinic in Shanghai. Amnestic MCI by Mayo criteria without biomarker confirmation. Community controls selected by an MMSE of 28 or more. Strict ocular and systemic exclusions. Small groups (23 MCI, 19 NC).

Time-domain Stratus OCT 3000 macular RNFL, with a derivation that is not clearly specified. Flash ERG on LKC UTAS-E 3000 with non-ISCEV stimulus descriptions in Td-s. Of the flash-ERG latencies, only the dark-adapted rod cone response latency separated MCI from controls.
